facts.fact: Closed-form similarity Procrustes (unweighted): center both point sets, form the cross-covariance matrix, take its SVD; rotation is V U^T with a determinant correction to exclude reflections; scale and translation follow in closed form from the same decomposition. Search summary of arXiv 2206.14528, not verified against the full text.
The optimal translation once rotation is known is the averaged residual between the centred target and rotated source, t = (1/n)(X2 - X1 R^T) 1 (sign/ordering depends on convention).
Procrustes with deformations has a closed-form solution via eigenvalue decomposition (paper title, 2022).

A geodesy paper reports that the symmetric case of weighted similarity transformation (weights on both coordinate systems) generally lacks a closed form and is solved iteratively, while asymmetric cases have closed forms.
Generalized Procrustes analysis across many shapes requires an iterative algorithm because the reference shape is updated at each step (per search summary of the geodesy/Procrustes sources).
Thin-plate spline mapping is a non-rigid, closed-form interpolant of corresponding landmarks, with kernel U(r) = r^2 ln r in 2D, and an affine part.

TPS bending energy is the integral of the squared Frobenius norm of the Hessian of the mapping, I = integral ||Hess T||_F^2 dx; TPS minimises this subject to interpolation and affine constraints (weights sum to zero, landmark-weighted sums zero).
Noisy landmarks: exact TPS interpolation can be relaxed by replacing K with K + lambda I; as lambda grows the solution approaches the affine map, which has zero bending energy.
Bookstein (1989) treats the bending energy as a quadratic form in the surface heights at the landmarks, and the TPS as a superposition of eigenvectors of the bending energy matrix.
Some patent sources use U(r) = r (not r^2 ln r) for a 3D TPS-style implant model; no single standard 3D kernel was confirmed.

ARAP (Sorkine & Alexa, SGP 2007): iterative mesh editing where each local neighbourhood is fit to its best rigid transform via a Procrustes problem, then vertex positions are updated by solving a linear system.

ARAP is described as effective and easy to implement; later work notes standard ARAP can produce spikes, motivating a higher-order smooth variant (Oehri, Herholz, Sorkine-Hornung, 2025) per search summary.
Finnendahl, Schwartz, Alexa ('ARAP Revisited') reinterpret ARAP as a discretised elastic energy; Igarashi et al. (JGT 2009) give an implementation guide and show ARAP for surface flattening.

Optimal-step non-rigid ICP (Amberg, Romdhani, Vetter, CVPR 2007) runs a sequence of decreasing stiffness weights, starting high, so the template moves from global to local deformation; it works with any regulariser that has an adjustable stiffness parameter.

Amberg et al. report that a general black-box optimiser performs poorly for non-rigid registration: it has a very small convergence basin and fails on incomplete surfaces unless initialisation is nearly perfect.

Dense face-scan tracking (arXiv 1709.04295) uses a stiffness weight alpha in a cost with landmark and motion-history terms; face-capture work (arXiv 2003.08583) describes gradually decreasing stiffness and landmark weights.
Botsch & Sorkine (2008) is a survey of linear variational mesh deformation methods aimed at detailed high-resolution meshes.

Biharmonic deformation uses solutions of the bi-Laplace equation, which also minimise a Laplacian energy; assigning identity handles does not reproduce the original surface unless it is already biharmonic.
Bounded biharmonic weights (Jacobson, Baran, Popovic, Sorkine, 2011) minimise Laplacian energy under bound constraints for real-time deformation.
Sorkine (2005) state-of-the-art report covers Laplacian mesh processing with differential coordinates; Lipman & Sorkine (2005) extend it to interactive mesh editing.
A 2021 review (arXiv 2103.01694) compares geometric and neural shape-editing techniques.

contradictions: Closed-form claim vs iterative claim: unweighted similarity Procrustes has a closed form via SVD, but weighted/symmetric variants (geodesy source) and generalized Procrustes (many shapes) are described as needing iteration.
TPS kernel: the 2D kernel r^2 ln r (Bookstein) differs from the U(r)=r variant seen in patent sources for 3D; the latter is not confirmed as a standard.
